correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the four rational-canonical types in the two-dimensional general linear group. For split semisimple matrices the tensor eigenvalues are listed explicitly and the only resonances are eigenvalue one, a directed squaring relation, and the order-three duplication. For irreducible quadratics, Frobenius conjugacy reduces the resonance to an element whose order divides both q-2 and q^2-1, hence to the unique nontrivial cube-root pair exactly when q is congruent to two modulo three. The nonsemisimple fixed-space ranks are controlled by explicit minors and row reduction. All class sizes and class counts sum to the exact general-linear-group order. The packaged exhaustive computation independently reconstructs every tensor matrix and matches the closed distribution over five fields, including the non-prime field of order four.

value.rationale: The result answers a concrete closed-form counting question explicitly posed in the motivating paper, uniformly for every finite field in the first nontrivial matrix dimension. It identifies exactly which fixed-space dimensions can occur and how characteristic two and cube-root arithmetic alter the distribution. The distribution is strictly finer than the already known number of algebra isomorphism classes and supplies a transparent Burnside decomposition of that classical total.
